A common weather pattern is the formation of thunderstorms. This starts with a warm, moist air mass rising up into cooler air. As it goes higher, it gets colder and starts to condense, forming clouds. If the temperature drops enough, water droplets in the air start to freeze, creating ice crystals. These ice crystals fall and collect more water droplets and more ice crystals as they go down through the cloud. This creates larger and larger droplets. Eventually, they get too heavy and fall out of the cloud as rain.
